article.title: There's Been a Major Shift in American-Syrian Policy
US removes Syria from state sponsor of terrorism list
article.summary: WASHINGTON: The United States on Monday delisted Syria as a state sponsor of terrorism, rescinding a decades-old designation that had severely impeded investment.The US Department of State also revoked its designation of al-Nusrah Front — also known as Hay’at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) — as a global terrorist organisation. The Treasury Department followed through with sanctions relief.“Today’s action will help foster additional investment in Syria to promote political and economic stability,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement.Treasury said the moves were “in line with President (Donald) Trump’s promise to deliver sanctions relief to Syria.” But the agency stressed that its removal of restrictions on Syria “does not change Treasury’s posture with regards to countering global terrorism and our commitment to hold bad actors in Syria accountable.”The HTS was earlier known as Al Nusra Front and was formerly the branch of Al Qaeda in Syria. article.title: Turkish envoy applauds US removal of Syria from 'terrorism list'
article.summary: Turkish envoy applauds US removal of Syria from 'terrorism list'Washington's decision to remove Syria from the State Sponsor of Terrorism (SST) blacklist paves the way for a "brighter future" for the country, Turkey's ambassador to Damascus said."The last obstacle standing in the way of our friend and brother Syria’s integration with the world has finally been removed," Nuh Yilmaz wrote on X."Syria's removal from the U.S. Department of State's list of countries supporting terrorism is not only important for Syria's normalization, stability, and development, but also an extremely significant decision for the stability and peace of the region."Yilmaz added that he hopes the move would "bring goodness to all the Syrian people and the Syrian state".

article.title: Ahmad al-Sharaa hails Syria's removal from US 'terrorism list'
article.summary: Ahmad al-Sharaa hails Syria's removal from US 'terrorism list'Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa has applauded his country's removal from the State Sponsor of Terrorism (SST) blacklist."Today, Syria is shedding a dark stain from its shoulders and tearing up with its own hands a page from its painful past, to move into a new space of development, reconstruction and building," he said in a video posted on X."Great people of Syria, you have done it again. Sanctions have been lifted from you and restrictions have been removed."He also congratulated Syrians for the latest US move and thanked Donald Trump for what he described as a "historic decision".

article.title: US removes Syria from terrorism sponsor list, lifting major investment obstacle
article.summary: By Feras DalateyDAMASCUS, Aug 24 (Reuters) - The United States removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism on Monday, lifting what Damascus says was the last major impediment to investing in the country as Washington deepens ties to the new Syrian government.The removal, posted on the U.S. Treasury's website, took effect after a 45-day congressional review period triggered when Trump formally notified Congress on July 8 of his intention to rescind the designation.

article.title: US removes Syria's designation as State Sponsor of Terrorism list
article.summary: Aug 24 (Reuters) - The State Department on Monday removed Syria from its list of State Sponsors of Terrorism, according to a notification from the U.S. Treasury, in a move that was first announced earlier this year pending a review by Congress.The designation as a state sponsor of terrorism carries restrictions on U.S. foreign assistance, defense exports and certain financial transactions.Monday's announcement also removed the designation of the Nusrah Front as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist organization.

article.title: US removes Syria from state sponsor of terrorism list
article.summary: The United States on Monday removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism, rescinding a decades-old designation that came with severe economic restrictions and marking another step in warming ties between the countries.The US Department of State also revoked its designation of al-Nusra Front -- latterly known as Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) -- as a global terrorist organization. The Treasury Department announced corresponding sanctions relief.
